Reproducing the manuscript numbers, tables, and figures

Companion to Three Routes to One Answer: Reconciling AIPW, TMLE, and Double Machine Learning for Applied Researchers

The figures and data-bearing tables of the manuscript prepared for arXiv version 2 (arXiv:2609.26142; v2 forthcoming) are regenerated below directly from the committed result CSVs, and a numeric audit checks the reported numbers against them; the Super Learner engine is not re-run here. Each figure is the PDF drawn by R/make_figures.R (the R scripts in R/figures/ and python/paper_figures.py), shown as a 200-dpi image; the three schematics (Figures 1, 3 and 4) use no data. The estimator code lives in R/; the results it produced are frozen in docs/data/. For the methods themselves, read the paper.

Double cross-fitting corrected (October 2026)

The double cross-fit (DC-AIPW, DC-TMLE) released with arXiv version 1 averaged the predictions of both role assignments, so the propensity and outcome models were not trained on disjoint folds. The engine now uses one fixed rotation (score fold v with g fit on fold v+1 and Q on fold v+2, mod 3), and every double-cross-fit result was rerun with the original fold seeds. The CSVs below carry the corrected rows; every other row is unchanged. The repository README lists the main corrected values.

To reproduce the CSVs from scratch instead (re-running the engine), see the scripts in R/, the repository README, and the data sources and computing environments at the end of this page.

## Stage the frozen CSVs in output/, where R/ihdp_contrasts.R reads and writes, and read them from
## there. Nothing below fits a model or touches raw microdata. The figures are the PDFs that
## R/render_page.R drew before rendering (output/figures/), shown as 200-dpi images.
dir.create("output", showWarnings = FALSE)
invisible(file.copy(list.files("data", full.names = TRUE), "output", overwrite = TRUE))

rd  <- function(f) read.csv(file.path("output", f), check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
kab <- function(x, ...) knitr::kable(x, ...)
fig <- function(name) knitr::include_graphics(file.path("..", "output", "figures", "png", paste0(name, ".png")))
## a numeric table as written by R/make_tables.R, without its title line (the heading gives it)
tab <- function(n) cat(readLines(file.path("..", "output", "tables", sprintf("table%02d.md", n)))[-(1:2)], sep = "\n")

The ten figures and the manuscript’s copies

R/render_page.R draws the ten figures, then compares each PDF with the manuscript’s copy in figures/reference/ (tools/compare_pdf.py): page count and page boxes, the page structure (content streams byte for byte, and every font and graphics resource they name), and both files rendered at 144 dpi. A pass needs Arial and the package versions in renv.lock and requirements.txt; elsewhere, --text-only is a limited fallback that compares the words only.

Figure 1 — NHEFS causal DAG

The hypothesized confounding structure (fig:dag), drawn by R/figures/fig_dag.R (no data): the nine baseline covariates X are common causes of quitting smoking (A) and weight change (Y), and form the adjustment set.

Figure 2 — NHEFS propensity overlap

fig:nhefs-overlap, drawn by R/figures/fig_overlap.R from data/nhefs_overlap_data.csv: the scores of the overlap diagnostic’s own fit. That fit was not seeded, so the file is the reference. The truncation audit of the analysis fits is below.

fig("nhefs_overlap")

cat(sprintf("propensity range: [%.3f, %.3f]\n", min(pp$pi), max(pp$pi)))
#> propensity range: [0.044, 0.759]

Figure 3 — One score, two choices, one target

fig:concept, drawn by python/paper_figures.py (no data): one Super Learner supplies both nuisances, which assemble one efficient influence function; a combination rule (rows) and a fitting scheme (columns) give the six doubly-robust estimators of one target.

fig:fitting-schemes, drawn by python/paper_figures.py (no data): which rows train the initial nuisance fits and which rows they predict, for the full-sample, single cross-fit (V = 5) and double cross-fit (V = 3) schemes.

Figure 9 — Overlap and the spread of the estimates

fig:positivity, drawn by python/paper_figures.py. The upper panels are densities of two diagnostic fits: the NHEFS scores of Figure 2 (data/nhefs_overlap_data.csv) and the seeded LaLonde/NSW–PSID diagnostic (data/positivity_overlap.csv, from part (1) of R/positivity_diagnostics.R). The clipped peak of the LaLonde comparison group, about 154, is the Gaussian kernel density at R’s default bandwidth on a fine grid; R’s density() at its default 512 points gives about 123. The lower panels are the eight estimates (data/nhefs_panel_table.csv, medians over 100 splits; data/results_all3.csv, one split).

Companion diagnostic: IHDP overlap

Not a manuscript figure. Step 5 of the manuscript cites it for the IHDP design’s overlap: the estimated-propensity densities of IHDP realization 1, from the seeded diagnostic data/positivity_overlap.csv.

library(ggplot2)
po <- rd("positivity_overlap.csv")
ih <- po[grepl("^IHDP", po$dataset), ]
ggplot(ih, aes(pi, fill = group)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5, colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(control = "#B8860B", treated = "#AA3377")) +
  labs(x = "estimated P(A = 1 | X), IHDP realization 1", y = "density", fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "top")
cat(sprintf("IHDP realization 1: %d treated, %d comparison; scores %.3f to %.3f\n",
            sum(ih$group == "treated"), sum(ih$group == "control"), min(ih$pi), max(ih$pi)))
#> IHDP realization 1: 139 treated, 608 comparison; scores 0.018 to 0.518

Repeated splits: how much a single split moves the estimate

Behind the r = 100 rows of Figures 5 and 6: the single-split estimates of each split-based route across the 100 splits (data/nhefs_reps_raw.csv, data/rhc_reps_raw.csv), and the RHC running medians (data/rhc_reps_table.csv; Step 5).

p  <- rd("nhefs_panel_table.csv")
nr <- rd("nhefs_reps_raw.csv"); rw <- rd("rhc_reps_raw.csv"); rt <- rd("rhc_reps_table.csv")
kab(data.frame(estimator = names(tapply(nr$estimate, nr$method, sd)),
               `NHEFS SD across splits (kg)` = round(tapply(nr$estimate, nr$method, sd), 3),
               check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL))
estimator NHEFS SD across splits (kg)
CV-TMLE 0.078
DC-AIPW 0.141
DC-TMLE 0.140
DML (cross-fit AIPW) 0.078 
full2 <- p$estimate[is.na(p$r) & p$estimator %in% c("AIPW (one-step)", "TMLE")]
spans <- tapply(nr$estimate, nr$rep, function(e) diff(range(c(e, full2))))
cat(sprintf("NHEFS six doubly-robust estimates on a single split: median span %.2f kg (IQR %.2f-%.2f)\n",
            median(spans), quantile(spans, .25), quantile(spans, .75)))
#> NHEFS six doubly-robust estimates on a single split: median span 0.15 kg (IQR 0.09-0.22)
settle <- function(s, tol = 0.001) { ok <- abs(s$estimate - s$estimate[s$r == 100]) < tol
  for (k in seq_along(ok)) if (all(ok[k:length(ok)])) return(s$r[k]); NA }
kab(do.call(rbind, lapply(split(rt, rt$method), function(s) { s <- s[order(s$r), ]
  data.frame(estimator = s$method[1], `r = 1` = round(s$estimate[s$r == 1], 4),
             `r = 100` = round(s$estimate[s$r == 100], 4),
             `SD across splits` = round(sd(rw$estimate[rw$method == s$method[1]]), 4),
             `within 0.001 from r =` = settle(s),
             `largest distance from r = 100` = round(max(abs(s$estimate - s$estimate[s$r == 100])), 4),
             `CI width growth (%)` = round(100 * (s$ci_width[s$r == 100] / s$ci_width[s$r == 1] - 1), 1),
             check.names = FALSE) })), row.names = FALSE)

RHC: in-sample vs out-of-fold residuals

data/rhc_residual_diagnostic.csv, from R/rhc_residual_diagnostic.R (Step 4): the original seed-1 RHC fits (real_application.R), full-sample and five-fold cross-fit, with the outcome model’s residual root-mean-square, the g-computation plug-in, and AIPW’s mean weighted correction. Figure 6 shows the same full-sample fit, but its split-based rows are the first of 100 splits and the median over them, so the seed-1 cross-fit AIPW here (0.044) differs from Figure 6’s DML (0.043). Without ground truth, the comparison does not establish which estimate is more accurate.

kab(transform(rd("rhc_residual_diagnostic.csv"), resid_rms = round(resid_rms, 3), gcomp = round(gcomp, 4),
              correction = round(correction, 4), aipw = round(aipw, 4)), row.names = FALSE)
scheme resid_rms gcomp correction aipw

IHDP: design, paired contrasts, and the aggregated check

All 50 IHDP realizations share one fixed set of 747 covariate profiles and treatment assignments; each realization’s target is the sample average of its own simulated effect contrast. The coverage in Figure 7 is therefore conditional on this design, for a sample-average target. The realizations are generated independently given the design, so the realization is the Monte Carlo unit. R/ihdp_contrasts.R recomputes the paired contrasts and the exploratory r = 20 check from data/grade_raw.csv; the chunk below runs it and confirms that it reproduces the committed CSVs.

gr <- rd("grade_raw.csv"); tr <- tapply(gr$truth, gr$realization, unique)
cat(sprintf("%d realizations x %d fold seeds; sample-average targets %.2f to %.2f\n",
            length(tr), length(unique(gr$seed)), min(tr), max(tr)))
#> 50 realizations x 20 fold seeds; sample-average targets 3.16 to 12.65
frozen_ct <- rd("ihdp_contrasts.csv"); frozen_pil <- rd("ihdp_aggregated_pilot.csv")
invisible(capture.output(source("../R/ihdp_contrasts.R")))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(rd("ihdp_contrasts.csv"), frozen_ct)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(rd("ihdp_aggregated_pilot.csv"), frozen_pil)))
kab(transform(frozen_ct, difference = round(difference, 4), paired_mcse = round(paired_mcse, 4), t = round(t, 2)))

Software reconciliation over 20 seeds

data/nhefs_matched_repeated.csv: the three implementations built on the paper’s Super Learner library (the hand-coded engine, tmle, and AIPW), each re-run with 20 seeds and an explicit 0.025 propensity bound. The single runs scatter (SD across seeds about 0.08 kg for a single five-fold cross-fit), but the medians agree to within 0.01 kg. The combined differences yield similar medians here; the effects of individual implementation choices are not isolated (Step 7).

mr <- rd("nhefs_matched_repeated.csv")
cols <- c("hand_DML","AIPW_pkg","tmle_pkg")
kab(data.frame(
  implementation = c("hand-coded engine (DML)", "AIPW package", "tmle package"),
  `median (kg)`  = round(sapply(mr[cols], median, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
  `SD across seeds` = round(sapply(mr[cols], sd, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
  check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL))
implementation median (kg) SD across seeds

AIPW package 3.39 0.082
tmle package 3.39 0.036

Supplementary: three-benchmark comparison (not in the manuscript)

data/results_all3.csv: one run of the full panel on IHDP realization 1, LaLonde/NSW-PSID, and Twins. Twins is not used in the manuscript and its double-cross-fit rows were not rerun after the correction, so the table has no double-cross-fit rows for Twins. For LaLonde the truth column holds the $1,794 experimental estimate, which concerns a different population; bias and coverage are shown only for IHDP and Twins.

r3 <- rd("results_all3.csv")
show <- r3[, c("dataset","estimator","nuisance","estimate","ci_lo","ci_hi","bias","covers")]
show$bias[grepl("psid", show$dataset, ignore.case = TRUE)] <- NA
show$covers[grepl("psid", show$dataset, ignore.case = TRUE)] <- NA
kab(transform(show, estimate = round(estimate, 3), ci_lo = round(ci_lo, 3),
              ci_hi = round(ci_hi, 3), bias = round(bias, 3)), row.names = FALSE)

The deterministic audit R/verify_numbers.R re-derives the data-bearing numbers in the manuscript from these same CSVs and diffs each against the printed value. A table with 0 FAIL means the paper and the committed results agree.

invisible(capture.output(source("../R/verify_numbers.R")))
cat(sprintf("%d checks: %d PASS, %d FAIL\n",
            nrow(res), sum(res$status == "PASS"), sum(res$status == "FAIL")))
#> 270 checks: 270 PASS, 0 FAIL
kab(res)

Data sources and computing environments

The manuscript’s Data and Code availability statements refer to this section and to the repository README. Nothing on this page reads the raw data: they are needed only to refit the analyses, and none of them is redistributed with the manuscript or here. The source’s terms of use apply to each dataset.

Dataset Source Files, under data/
NHEFS (Hernán and Robins, 2020) the nhefs data of the causaldata R package (version 0.1.4 on CRAN) none
Right-heart catheterization (Connors et al., 1996) Vanderbilt’s CSV export of the RHC dataset, rhc.csv, from the Right Heart Catheterization Dataset page of hbiostat.org (https://hbiostat.org/data/repo/rhc.csv). The file analysed is byte-identical to that download (2,320,412 bytes; checked 2026-11-02). The dr3 loader instead retrieves the R-format export through Hmisc::getHdata(), which differs slightly. rhc/rhc.csv
LaLonde/NSW–PSID (LaLonde, 1986; Dehejia and Wahba, 1999) the Dehejia–Wahba experimental sample, nsw_dw.dta, and the PSID comparison sample, psid_controls.dta, from https://users.nber.org/~rdehejia/nswdata2.html lalonde_nsw/nsw_dw.dta, lalonde_nsw/psid_controls.dta
IHDP semi-synthetic benchmark (Hill, 2011) realizations 1–50, ihdp_npci_1.csv to ihdp_npci_50.csv, from https://github.com/claudiashi57/dragonnet, folder dat/ihdp/csv/ at commit 2e51b24788 ihdp/ihdp_npci_1.csv to ihdp/ihdp_npci_50.csv
Twins (supplementary; Louizos et al., 2017) data/Twin_data.csv.gz from https://github.com/jsyoon0823/GANITE at commit e2997317d5 twins/Twin_data.csv.gz

Fits that were not seeded. The NHEFS propensity-overlap diagnostic (data/nhefs_overlap_data.csv) and the full-sample fits of the IHDP grading (data/grade_raw.csv) were not seeded per unit, so a rerun gives slightly different values; for these fits, the archived files are the reference. Rerunning R/grade_ihdp.R for realization 1 and fold seed 1 on the workstation reproduced both double-cross-fit rows exactly and the other six rows to within 0.04.

Refitting. Refitting a stochastic analysis from the raw data need not reproduce the archived values exactly. Super Learner fits depend on learner-package versions and on the computing platform, and the rows from the cluster jobs cannot be guaranteed to regenerate exactly, because that environment’s package versions are unknown.
